ego.name: Douglas Engelbart
ego.summary: Douglas Engelbart was an American engineer and inventor who pioneered interactive computing and human–computer interaction. At SRI International he founded the Augmentation Research Center and led development of the oN-Line System (NLS), showcased in the 1968 “Mother of All Demos,” introducing and integrating concepts such as the computer mouse, hypertext, and collaborative on-screen editing.

category_summaries.summary: Engelbart’s family circle includes his parents Carl and Gladys, siblings Dorianne and David, his wife Ballard Fish, and his daughter Christina—who became a key late-life partner in advancing his mission.

Centered on SRI’s Augmentation Research Center: close builders like Bill English and Jeff Rulifson, early colleague Hewitt Crane, and funders/decision-makers (Rowena Swanson, J. C. R. Licklider, Robert Taylor, Bertram Raphael) who shaped what the lab could do.
Engelbart’s direction was catalyzed by earlier thinkers—especially Vannevar Bush—while later web-era recognition connected him to figures such as Tim Berners-Lee.
A small social/presentation layer surrounds the 1968 demo, including Stewart Brand’s advice on how to communicate the team’s work to a broad audience.
